holidayDescriptions.new_years_day: New Year's Day marks the start of the Gregorian calendar year and is a public holiday in most countries.
holidayDescriptions.christmas_day: Christmas Day is a Christian holiday celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ, observed on December 25.
holidayDescriptions.independence_day: Independence Day commemorates the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.
holidayDescriptions.thanksgiving: Thanksgiving is celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November in the United States, a day of giving thanks for the harvest.
holidayDescriptions.labor_day: Labor Day honors the contributions of workers and the labor movement, observed on the first Monday in September.
holidayDescriptions.memorial_day: Memorial Day is a federal holiday honoring military personnel who have died in service, observed on the last Monday in May.
holidayDescriptions.juneteenth: Juneteenth commemorates June 19, 1865, when enslaved people in Texas learned of their freedom, two years after the Emancipation Proclamation.
holidayDescriptions.martin_luther_king_jr_day: Martin Luther King Jr. Day honors the civil rights leader born on January 15, 1929.
holidayDescriptions.presidents_day: Presidents' Day honors all U.S. presidents, with particular emphasis on George Washington and Abraham Lincoln.
holidayDescriptions.columbus_day: Columbus Day marks the anniversary of Christopher Columbus's arrival in the Americas on October 12, 1492.
holidayDescriptions.veterans_day: Veterans Day honors all military veterans who have served in the United States Armed Forces.
holidayDescriptions.good_friday: Good Friday commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his death at Calvary.
holidayDescriptions.easter_monday: Easter Monday is the day after Easter Sunday, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
holidayDescriptions.boxing_day: Boxing Day, observed on December 26, is a holiday in the UK, Australia, and Canada with origins in giving to the poor.
holidayDescriptions.australia_day: Australia Day on January 26 marks the anniversary of the 1788 arrival of the First Fleet at Port Jackson.
holidayDescriptions.anzac_day: Anzac Day on April 25 commemorates Australian and New Zealand Army Corps soldiers who served in the Gallipoli Campaign.
holidayDescriptions.canada_day: Canada Day on July 1 celebrates the anniversary of Canadian Confederation in 1867.
holidayDescriptions.victoria_day: Victoria Day is a Canadian federal holiday celebrated on the last Monday before May 25, honoring Queen Victoria.
holidayDescriptions.remembrance_day: Remembrance Day on November 11 honors Canadian and Commonwealth military members who died in wars.
holidayDescriptions.삼일절: March 1st Movement Day commemorates the 1919 independence movement against Japanese colonial rule in Korea.
holidayDescriptions.어린이날: Children's Day on May 5 is a Korean national holiday dedicated to the happiness and welfare of children.
holidayDescriptions.현충일: Memorial Day on June 6 honors Korean patriots and soldiers who died for the country.
holidayDescriptions.광복절: Liberation Day on August 15 commemorates Korea's liberation from Japanese colonial rule in 1945.
holidayDescriptions.개천절: National Foundation Day on October 3 celebrates the legendary founding of the first Korean kingdom by Dangun.
holidayDescriptions.한글날: Hangul Day on October 9 celebrates the creation of the Korean alphabet by King Sejong the Great.
holidayDescriptions.설날: Seollal is the Korean Lunar New Year, one of the most important traditional Korean holidays.
holidayDescriptions.추석: Chuseok is the Korean harvest festival, celebrated on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month.
holidayDescriptions.부처님오신날: Buddha's Birthday celebrates the birth of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism.
holidayDescriptions.元日: New Year's Day (Ganjitsu) marks the beginning of the new year and is celebrated on January 1 in Japan.
holidayDescriptions.成人の日: Coming-of-Age Day (Seijin no Hi) honors those who have turned 20 years old during the past year.
holidayDescriptions.建国記念の日: National Foundation Day (Kenkoku Kinen no Hi) on February 11 commemorates the legendary founding of Japan.
holidayDescriptions.天皇誕生日: The Emperor's Birthday (Tenno Tanjobi) is a national holiday celebrating the reigning Emperor's birthday on February 23.
holidayDescriptions.春分の日: Vernal Equinox Day (Shunbun no Hi) is a Japanese holiday celebrating the coming of spring.
holidayDescriptions.昭和の日: Showa Day (Showa no Hi) on April 29 honors Emperor Showa and reflects on Japan's turbulent Showa era.
holidayDescriptions.憲法記念日: Constitution Memorial Day (Kenpo Kinenbi) on May 3 commemorates the enactment of the Japanese Constitution in 1947.
holidayDescriptions.みどりの日: Greenery Day (Midori no Hi) on May 4 is a Japanese holiday celebrating nature and greenery.
holidayDescriptions.こどもの日: Children's Day (Kodomo no Hi) on May 5 is a Japanese national holiday celebrating the happiness of children.
holidayDescriptions.海の日: Marine Day (Umi no Hi) is a Japanese holiday giving thanks to the ocean and its bounty, observed on the third Monday of July.
holidayDescriptions.山の日: Mountain Day (Yama no Hi) on August 11 is a Japanese holiday to appreciate mountains and their nature.
holidayDescriptions.敬老の日: Respect for the Aged Day (Keiro no Hi) honors elderly citizens who have contributed to society, observed on the third Monday of September.
holidayDescriptions.秋分の日: Autumnal Equinox Day (Shubun no Hi) is a Japanese holiday for commemorating ancestors and honoring the deceased.
holidayDescriptions.スポーツの日: Sports Day (Supotsu no Hi) promotes healthy, active lifestyles and is observed on the second Monday of October.
holidayDescriptions.文化の日: Culture Day (Bunka no Hi) on November 3 celebrates freedom, peace, and the promotion of culture.
holidayDescriptions.勤労感謝の日: Labour Thanksgiving Day (Kinro Kansha no Hi) on November 23 celebrates labour and production and gives thanks.

studyPlanner.faq1q: What is a printable study planner 2026?
studyPlanner.faq1a: A printable study planner is a monthly calendar you download as a PDF and print at home. It gives you a physical grid to write in exam dates, assignment deadlines, and study blocks — without needing an app or an account.
studyPlanner.faq2q: How do I use a free study schedule template effectively?
studyPlanner.faq2a: Start by filling in fixed commitments: exam dates, submission deadlines, and class times. Then work backwards to schedule study blocks. Print one month at a time so you can annotate directly on paper. Many students colour-code by subject.
studyPlanner.faq3q: Do the study planner calendars include public holidays?
studyPlanner.faq3a: Yes. Every calendar includes official public holidays for your chosen country (USA, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, or South Korea), so you never accidentally schedule a study session on a day your library or campus is closed.
studyPlanner.faq4q: Can I download a study planner for a specific month?
studyPlanner.faq4a: Yes. Choose any month and country from the grid above, then click View to preview or PDF to download instantly. No login or payment is required.
studyPlanner.faq5q: What paper size are the study planner PDFs?
studyPlanner.faq5a: All calendars download as A4 landscape PDF. They also print well on US Letter paper with minimal scaling. The clean, minimal design works in both colour and black-and-white.
